# IVR TTS

Outbound voice-message dialer for [FreeSWITCH](https://freeswitch.org/) / [FusionPBX](https://www.fusionpbx.com/).

Upload a CSV with contacts, and the dialer calls each one and plays a personalized text-to-speech
(TTS) message — for example, a payment reminder for a condominium unit. Every call result
(job status, hangup cause, SIP failure code) is stored in PostgreSQL.

**API documentation:** `http://<server_ip>:8000/docs` (Swagger UI generated by FastAPI)

## How it works

```text
           CSV upload                      bgapi originate               dialplan ext. "99"
 client ───────────────► app.py ──► DB ◄── dialer.py ──────────► FreeSWITCH ──────────────────┐
         (OAuth2/Fief)   (FastAPI)  │          ▲  ESL inbound (8021)                          │
                                    │          └── BACKGROUND_JOB / CHANNEL_HANGUP events     │
                                    │                                                         ▼
                                    └──────────────── tts_voice_message.py ◄── socket (ESL outbound :5000)
                                                      speaks the message via mod_unimrcp, hangs up
```

The application is made of three processes, all started by `run.sh`:

| Process | File | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web server | `ivr_tts/app.py` | FastAPI app. `POST /v1/upload_csv` validates the CSV and phone numbers and inserts rows into `big_table_input`. Protected by OAuth2 through [Fief](https://www.fief.dev/). |
| Dialer | `ivr_tts/dialer.py` | Connects to FreeSWITCH through ESL (inbound), picks rows with no `job_uuid` and originates calls (up to `dialer_max_concurrent_calls` at once). Stores job status and hangup cause on each row. |
| IVR server | `ivr_tts/tts_voice_message.py` | ESL outbound socket server on port 5000. FreeSWITCH hands each answered call to it; it loads the contact row (via the `data_id` channel variable), speaks the message and hangs up. The result is written to `big_table_output`. |

Other modules:

- `ivr_tts/settings.py` — configuration (pydantic-settings).
- `ivr_tts/models.py` — SQLAlchemy models. Run it as a script to (re)create the schema.
- `ivr_tts/freeswitch.py` — wrapper around the greenswitch ESL connection (originate, reconnect).
- `ivr_tts/csv_import.py` — command-line CSV import, without the API.
- `ivr_tts/listener.py` and `ivr_tts/stuff/` — debugging tools and older IVR flows (e.g. speech recognition yes/no prompts). Not used in production.

### CSV format

No header, one contact per line, columns `customer_name, condo, unity, phone`.
Phone numbers are parsed as Brazilian numbers (`phonenumbers`, region `BR`) and stored in national format.
See [`csv/example.csv`](csv/example.csv):

```csv
Fulano de Tal,Condomínio Exemplo,Bloco A 101,(11) 90000-0001
```

## Configuration

Settings are read from environment variables or from `etc/.env` (relative to the working directory).
Start from the example:

```bash
cp etc/.env.example etc/.env
```

| Setting | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `freeswitch_host` / `_port` / `_password` | `localhost` / `8021` / `ClueCon` | ESL inbound connection |
| `freeswitch_keep_connected` | `2` | seconds between connection checks |
| `freeswitch_connection_max_retry` | `0` | connection attempts, `0` = infinite |
| `freeswitch_connection_wait_retry` | `3` | seconds between connection attempts |
| `dialer_domain` | **required** | domain used on originate (`loopback/<phone>/<domain>`) |
| `dialer_dialplan_context` | **required** | dialplan context of the IVR extension |
| `dialer_dialplan_dst` | **required** | IVR extension number (e.g. `99`) |
| `dialer_max_concurrent_calls` | `10` | simultaneous calls |
| `dialer_job_wait_time` | `10` | seconds to wait when there is nothing to dial |
| `dialer_callerid_number` / `_name` | `0000` / `IVR TTS Dialer` | caller ID on originated calls |
| `ivr_company_name` | `Example Company` | company name spoken on the message |
| `ivr_contact_phone` | `zero oitocentos, …` | contact phone, written **as it must be spoken** |
| `postgres_host` / `_port` / `_user` / `_password` / `_database` | `localhost` / `5432` / `ivr_tts` / – / `ivr_tts` | database |
| `database_url` | built from `postgres_*` | full SQLAlchemy URL, overrides `postgres_*` |
| `fief_base_url` | `https://auth.example.com` | Fief server |
| `fief_client_id` / `fief_client_secret` | **required** | Fief OAuth2 client |

The upload endpoint requires the `campaing:csv:write` permission on the Fief access token.

The TTS message itself is in `TTSVoiceMessage.safe_run()` (`ivr_tts/tts_voice_message.py`), in Brazilian Portuguese,
using `unimrcp:uni2` and voice `pt-BR-Wavenet-B` (Google Cloud TTS through UniMRCP). Adjust it to your use case.

## Development

Requires Python 3.12+ and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```bash
uv sync                 # install dependencies (including dev)
uv run pytest           # run the test suite (no FreeSWITCH or PostgreSQL needed)
```

Running the processes locally (from the repository root, with `etc/.env` configured):

```bash
uv run python ivr_tts/models.py                    # create the schema (drops existing tables!)
uv run uvicorn --app-dir ivr_tts app:app --reload  # web server
uv run python ivr_tts/dialer.py                    # dialer
uv run python ivr_tts/tts_voice_message.py         # IVR server
```

## Deployment

### 1. Install git and Docker

```bash
apt -y install git docker.io        # Debian/Ubuntu
yum -y install git docker           # RHEL/CentOS
systemctl enable --now docker
```

Full docs: <https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/>

### 2. Allow ESL connections from the Docker network

By default FreeSWITCH only accepts ESL connections from localhost. Find the Docker bridge network:

```bash
ip a s docker0
# inet 172.17.0.1/16 scope global docker0
```

Edit `/etc/freeswitch/autoload_configs/event_socket.conf.xml`:

```xml
<configuration name="event_socket.conf" description="Socket Client">
  <settings>
    <param name="nat-map" value="false"/>
    <param name="listen-ip" value="0.0.0.0"/>
    <param name="listen-port" value="8021"/>
    <param name="password" value="ClueCon"/>
    <param name="apply-inbound-acl" value="rfc1918"/>
  </settings>
</configuration>
```

> **Change the default `ClueCon` password** whenever ESL listens on a non-loopback interface.

Make sure the `rfc1918` ACL allows the Docker network (`allow 172.17.0.0/16`). On FusionPBX this is under
*Advanced > Access Controls*. On older FreeSWITCH versions the ACL is called `lan`.

```bash
fs_cli -x reloadacl
fs_cli -x 'reload mod_event_socket'
```

### 3. Create the IVR dialplan extension

The dialer originates `loopback/<phone>/<dialer_domain>` and bridges it to `dialer_dialplan_dst` in
`dialer_dialplan_context`. That extension must hand the call to the IVR server (container IP, port 5000):

```xml
<extension name="ivr_tts" continue="false">
  <condition field="destination_number" expression="^99$">
    <action application="socket" data="172.17.0.2:5000 full"/>
  </condition>
</extension>
```

The TTS engine (`mod_unimrcp` with a profile named `uni2`) must be configured on FreeSWITCH.

### 4. Set up PostgreSQL

Make PostgreSQL listen on the Docker interface (`postgresql.conf`):

```text
listen_addresses = 'localhost, 172.17.0.1'
```

Allow the Docker network (`pg_hba.conf`) and restart:

```text
host    all     all     172.17.0.0/16       scram-sha-256
```

```bash
systemctl restart postgresql
su - postgres -c "psql -c \"CREATE USER ivr_tts WITH PASSWORD '<complex_password>';\""
su - postgres -c "psql -c 'CREATE DATABASE ivr_tts OWNER ivr_tts;'"
```

### 5. Firewall

The containers must reach the host through the bridge network:

```bash
# firewalld
firewall-cmd --permanent --zone=trusted --change-interface=docker0 && firewall-cmd --reload
# iptables
iptables -I INPUT -i docker0 -j ACCEPT && iptables-save > /etc/iptables/rules.v4
```

### 6. Build and run

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<your-user>/ivr-tts.git /usr/src/ivr-tts
cd /usr/src/ivr-tts
docker build -t ivr-tts .

mkdir -p /etc/ivr-tts
cp etc/.env.example /etc/ivr-tts/.env
vim /etc/ivr-tts/.env        # freeswitch_host / postgres_host = 172.17.0.1, passwords, domain...
```

Create the database schema on the first run:

```bash
docker run --rm -v /etc/ivr-tts:/opt/ivr-tts/etc ivr-tts python ivr_tts/models.py
```

Start the service:

```bash
docker run -d --restart=unless-stopped --log-driver=journald --name=ivr-tts \
  -v /etc/ivr-tts:/opt/ivr-tts/etc -p 8000:8000 ivr-tts
```

The container exposes the API on port 8000 over plain HTTP. Put it behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy
(nginx, Caddy, Traefik...) before exposing it to the internet.

Useful switches: `-it --entrypoint /bin/bash` opens a shell instead of `run.sh` (debugging),
`-v` mounts a volume, `-p` publishes a port, `-d` runs in background.
